skills.name: Prepare and describe the oxides of nitrogen

note.text:
Three oxides of nitrogen are studied.
• Dinitrogen oxide, N2O ('laughing gas'): made by gently heating ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3 → N2O + 2H2O. Colourless, faintly sweet, fairly soluble, neutral. It relights a glowing splint, like oxygen, because it decomposes on the hot splint. Used with oxygen as a mild anaesthetic.
• Nitrogen oxide, NO: made by warming copper with dilute nitric acid. Colourless and neutral, almost insoluble in water, but it turns brown at once in air: 2NO + O2 → 2NO2. That is the test for it.
• Nitrogen dioxide, NO2: made by heating lead(II) nitrate, or by copper with concentrated nitric acid. A brown, poisonous, acidic gas, denser than air, very soluble: 2NO2 + H2O → HNO3 + HNO2.
Nitrogen oxides from car engines and lightning take part in acid rain.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to prepare and recognise the three oxides of nitrogen and tell them apart by colour and by simple tests.
Builds on: Lesson {14} (nitrates give oxides of nitrogen on heating) and Lesson {13} (nitric acid with copper).
Leads to: Lesson {16} (the nitrogen cycle) and the part these oxides play in acid rain.

key_words.meaning: a substance that takes away the feeling of pain
an oxide that gives an acid with water
a haze formed when sunlight acts on pollutants in the air

mistake.wrong: a gas that relights a glowing splint must be oxygen
mistake.right: it could also be dinitrogen oxide
mistake.why: {formula('N2O')} decomposes on the hot splint and gives oxygen, so it relights it too.

worked_example.problem: A colourless gas relights a glowing splint. Give two gases it could be, and a test that tells them apart.
steps: Dinitrogen oxide also relights one, because it decomposes on the hot splint to give oxygen.
To tell them apart, mix the gas with nitrogen oxide, {formula('NO')}.
With oxygen the mixture turns brown at once, because {2}{formula('NO')} + {formula('O2')} → {2}{formula('NO2')}; with {formula('N2O')} it does not.
worked_example.answer: oxygen or dinitrogen oxide; mixing with {formula('NO')} turns brown only with oxygen

cards.idea: {formula('N2O')} comes from gently heating ammonium nitrate and relights a glowing splint.
{formula('NO')} is colourless but turns brown at once in air.
{formula('NO2')} is brown and acidic: with water it gives nitric and nitrous acids.

w: By adding water to a nitride
e: A metal nitrate gives {formula('NO2')} and oxygen, not {formula('N2O')}.
Nitrogen does not burn in air.
A nitride with water gives ammonia.

pick.q: What is unusual about dinitrogen oxide in a test for gases?
pick.r: It relights a glowing splint, like oxygen
e: Limewater is the test for carbon dioxide.
That smell belongs to hydrogen sulphide.
{formula('N2O')} is colourless; {formula('NO2')} is the brown one.
pick.y: It decomposes on the hot splint to give oxygen, so it relights it; but it is not oxygen, and it has a faint sweet smell.

pick.q: Nitrogen oxide, {formula('NO')}, is let out into the air. What is seen?
e: It reacts with the oxygen of the air immediately.
It does not disappear; it becomes a visible brown gas.
pick.y: {2}{formula('NO')} + {formula('O2')} → {2}{formula('NO2')}: the brown colour is a test for {formula('NO')}.

pick.q: Which oxide of nitrogen is brown?
e: {formula('NO')} is colourless until it meets air.
pick.y: {formula('NO2')} is a brown, poisonous, acidic gas.

pick.q: Nitrogen dioxide is dissolved in water. What is formed?
pick.r: A mixture of nitric acid and nitrous acid
e: Ammonia is alkaline and is not formed from {formula('NO2')} and water.
The solution turns blue litmus red, so it is acidic.
The gas dissolves and reacts; it does not split into its elements.

pick.q: Which oxide of nitrogen is used as an anaesthetic?
e: {formula('NO')} is poisonous and is not used as an anaesthetic.
{formula('NO2')} is poisonous and damages the lungs.
{formula('N2O')} has been used in dentistry for many years.
pick.y: Dinitrogen oxide, 'laughing gas', is used with oxygen as a mild anaesthetic.

questions.prompt: Match each oxide of nitrogen to a property.

pool.right: Makes up most of the air

pick.q: How can nitrogen oxide be told from dinitrogen oxide?
pick.r: Nitrogen oxide turns brown when it meets air; dinitrogen oxide does not
pick.w1: Dinitrogen oxide turns brown in air
pick.w3: Neither can be told from the other

pick.q: How is nitrogen oxide prepared in the laboratory?
pick.r: By warming copper with dilute nitric acid
pick.w1: By warming copper with concentrated nitric acid
pick.y: The dilute acid is reduced as far as {formula('NO')}; the concentrated acid gives {formula('NO2')}.

pick.q: Why is nitrogen oxide collected over water?
pick.r: It is almost insoluble in water, and water keeps the air away from it
pick.w1: It is very soluble in water
pick.w2: It is less dense than air
pick.w3: It reacts with water to give an acid
pick.y: Collecting it over water stops it meeting air and turning brown.

questions.prompt: What volume of dinitrogen oxide, in dm³ at s.t.p., is given off when {n} mol of ammonium nitrate is gently heated?

misconceptions.explain: {2} is the coefficient of the WATER, not of the gas collected.
The question asks for a volume in dm³, not a mass in grams.

questions.prompt: What mass of ammonium nitrate, in grams, is needed to make {n} mol of dinitrogen oxide?

misconceptions.explain: The question asks for the mass of the SALT, not of the gas.

solution: {formula('NH4NO3')} → {formula('N2O')} + {2}{formula('H2O')}: {1} mol of the salt gives {1} mol of gas.
The relative formula mass of {formula('NH4NO3')} is {molarMass('NH4NO3')}.
